date.as_written: saṃvat 1842 kā mārgaśiramāse kṛṣnapakṣe kṛṣṇai navamyā (!) tithau śukravāre

notes: 'indrasīha' = Indrasiṃha (the anusvāra is dropped, Nepali-style spelling). The catalogue gives Indrasiṃha as the scribe. The colophon itself only says the copy is for his reading ('indrasīhapāthārthaṃ' = pāṭhārthaṃ). The preceding 'ma' may be a corrupt 'mayā' ('by me'); in that case he is the scribe and copied for his own study, so his roles would be scribe + owner. The 'saṃvat' era is not named. It is taken as VS, which fits a Nepalese Devanagari manuscript dated 1842, so the date falls in Nov/Dec 1785 CE. 'navamyā' stands for navamyāṃ. 'subhathāne' = śubhasthāne. 'Śivapurī' is not securely identified; it may be Shivapuri near Kathmandu. '46' after the section colophon is probably a verse count.
